title: Ropedia Xperience 2: 1,589 Scans, 131 Hours Robot Video
summary: Ropedia Xperience 2 ships 1,589 metric-scale 3D scans and 131 hours of egocentric task video across 596 locations for robot learning and retargeting.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Ropedia released Xperience 2 with 1,589 3D scans and 131 hours of human task video across 596 locations on November 13, 2026.
- The dataset enables robot motion retargeting with 0.40 to 0.55 cm median hand error and 100% physical constraint satisfaction in simulation.
- Gemini-2.5-Pro reached 74.2% on spatial intelligence tasks, but frontier models struggled on long-horizon contact-rich robot control benchmarks.


Ropedia officially launched Xperience 2 on November 13, 2026, pairing 1,589 metric-scale 3D scans with 4,230 egocentric task recordings totaling 131 hours across 596 collection sites. The dataset targets robot-learning systems that struggle with long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation tasks in real-world environments, offering a bridge from human demonstration to robot execution.


## Dataset Structure and Collection Method


Xperience 2 captures 74 distinct task types using a handheld LiDAR scanner for geometry and a head-mounted multi-camera rig named HOMIE for egocentric video. The release leans heavily residential: 1,389 of the scans, representing 87.4% of the dataset, come from home interiors. Each recording places geometry, video, camera poses, hand motion, and body pose in a shared metric frame, enabling direct real-to-sim conversion without manual alignment.


The authors frame the approach as operator-scaling rather than robot-scaling. Capture runs at human speed without requiring on-site robot deployment, and the captured data can be expanded into robot trajectories without additional field collection. The registration pipeline handles synchronization across modalities and outputs data ready for trajectory generation, virtual teleoperation, and motion retargeting.


## Spatial Intelligence and Detection Benchmarks


Three benchmarks accompany the dataset. On a 500-question spatial-intelligence slice, Gemini-2.5-Pro leads at 74.2% overall accuracy and GPT-6 Astra High trails at 71.8%. Performance drops sharply on specific subtasks: no model exceeds 34% on distance questions or 55% on translation questions. The fragility suggests frontier models have not yet generalized spatial reasoning to real-world clutter.


For 3D object detection on the same scenes, results are stark. Boxer leads across all three evaluation metrics, while competing methods stay below 7 AP at the 0.25 IoU threshold. LLaVA-3D and SceneScript produce no bounding box that reaches 0.25 IoU, and no method clears 7 AP at the stricter 0.50 threshold. The benchmarks highlight a gap between vision-language model performance on static question-answering and structured prediction in metric 3D space.


## Human-to-Robot Motion Retargeting Results


The dataset demonstration converts captured human motion to a wheeled humanoid platform. Median hand-tracking error lands between 0.40 and 0.55 cm, and retargeted trajectories satisfy physical constraints in 100% of frames. An eight-subtask kitchen-to-bedroom routine completes 30 of 30 simulated rollouts without task violations, covering actions from microwave manipulation to door opening and object placement.


The retargeting pipeline takes human fingertip traces and body kinematics and solves for joint angles that respect the robot's mechanical limits. The low error margins and perfect constraint satisfaction suggest the registration pipeline preserves enough spatial fidelity for closed-loop control, though real-world deployment results are not reported in the release.


## Release Date and Competitive Context


Officially released on November 13, 2026, Xperience 2 enters a crowded robotics-data landscape. The release lands one day after Runway's Praxis-1 open release and follows 205 robotics stories tracked in the prior 90 days. The dataset's focus on residential environments and egocentric human demonstration distinguishes it from simulation-heavy datasets and teleoperated robot collections.


The paper positions Xperience 2 against foundation models recently adapted for direct robot control, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1. The authors note these models remain brittle on long-horizon tasks, and the dataset's benchmark results support that claim: even the highest-scoring model, Gemini-2.5-Pro, fails on distance and translation reasoning, and all tested methods collapse on 3D detection.


## What This Means


Xperience 2 provides a large-scale, metrically registered dataset for robot learning, but the accompanying benchmarks expose persistent gaps in spatial reasoning and object detection for frontier models. The human-to-robot retargeting results demonstrate technical feasibility at centimeter-scale accuracy, yet the lack of real-world rollout data leaves open questions about sim-to-real transfer. As labs push toward general-purpose robot control, datasets like Xperience 2 will test whether scaling data diversity can close the gap between language-model reasoning and physical task execution.
